subject.title: Session lane starvation: followup drain monopolizes session lane, blocks inbound dispatch for 20-30min

question: Which scheduling invariant should OpenClaw enforce when active follow-up work and fresh user/control work compete for the same session lane?
rationale: The source-reproducible bug is clear, but the durable fix changes cross-channel queue ordering and STOP/control semantics, so automation should not choose the product policy alone.

options.title: Foreground Wins
options.body: Define fresh user messages and control actions as higher-priority work that can interrupt or bypass follow-up drains while preserving transcript consistency.

options.title: Bound Follow-Up Drains
options.body: Keep the current model but cap consecutive follow-up drains and yield between batches so queued foreground work gets admission opportunities.

options.title: Broader Lane Redesign
options.body: Fold this into a larger two-lane or per-channel scheduling design with explicit background lanes for compaction, browser, cron, and follow-up work.

recommendation.title: Foreground Wins
recommendation.body: Define fresh user messages and control actions as higher-priority work that can interrupt or bypass follow-up drains while preserving transcript consistency.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history on adjacent reply-queue and foreground-delivery fixes.
